correctness.rationale: Each multipartite part is monochromatic because its vertices have the same open neighborhood. Writing global color totals gives exact closed-neighborhood balance equations. Comparing two differently colored parts forces both to be singletons, with separate valid arguments for \(k=2\) and \(k\ge3\); comparing any remaining same-colored part to a singleton then forces it to be a singleton too. The graph is therefore \(K_r\), and balance reduces exactly to equal global color-class sizes. The direct-definition verifier exhaustively agrees on \(583627\) small labeled assignments.
